study type: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Planned delivery at different gestational weeks (37, 38, 39 weeks) compared to expectant management
outcome: Maternal composite outcome (death, serious morbidity, preeclampsia with severe features, hemorrhage, abruption)
Neonatal composite outcome (fetal/neonatal death, respiratory support, low Apgar, neonatal seizures, suspected sepsis)
cohort: 1,417 pregnant individuals with mild chronic hypertension (both new diagnosis and preexisting), carrying term, singleton gestations, excluding those with fetal anomalies or preeclampsia before 37 weeks.
finding: Planned delivery in the early-Term period (37 or 38 weeks) compared with expectant management was not associated with a reduction in primary maternal or neonatal composite outcomes, but was associated with increased odds of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (at 37 weeks) and neonatal hypoglycemia (at 37 and 38 weeks).
gest_age: Term gestations (37 weeks or more) for participants, with delivery timing analyzed at 37, 38, and 39 weeks.
